children: Monro's board has suspended dividend payments as the provider of automotive repair and tire services continues to review strategic alternatives amid a challenging operating environment.

Monro, which had been paying a 28-cent quarterly dividend, said it has adequate liquidity to fund its operations and invest in initiatives that include driving profitable customer acquisition and increasing merchandising productivity.
Monro's dividend had represented an annual yield of nearly 12% based on Friday's closing price of $9.50.
Shares of the Fairport, N.Y., company, were recently down 6.7% to $8.85 in premarket trading.
Monro, which in May said it would look at options including a potential sale, said its board is still evaluating a range of alternatives.
The company in late October reported disappointing quarterly results, saying consumers have been deferring higher-ticket spending decisions and trading down to lower cost alternatives in tires.
